root_causes: Inefficient use of time: after the task was effectively completed, the agents continued executing low-value exploratory and wait actions (e.g., repeated Wait and Explore[kitchen_1]) instead of terminating promptly.
Lack of termination condition sensitivity: the policy did not trigger an early stop once all propositions were satisfied, leading to unnecessary extra steps and cumulative negative reward.

Redundant exploration behavior: Agent 1 repeatedly explored the same region of the kitchen despite the task being associated with the entryway bench, indicating insufficient coupling between object-search strategy and current task completion state.
improvement_suggestions: Introduce or strengthen an early-termination check that halts the episode immediately once all task propositions (mug, squeezer, toy food on bench_51) are satisfied.
Penalize or de-prioritize repeated, low-information exploration of the same room/region after task completion signals are detected to reduce redundant actions.
Modify the planner to dynamically re-evaluate goals so that once the goal state is reached, further exploration or waiting actions are suppressed.
Incorporate a success-detection mechanism tied to environment state (not just rewards) that, when triggered, transitions the policy to a dedicated ‘task complete’ state with no further motion.
Adjust the reward function to impose stronger penalties for unnecessary post-completion actions, encouraging agents to seek termination when no further improvement is possible.
overall_assessment: The task ultimately succeeded and reached 100% completion, but the execution was inefficient due to many redundant wait and exploration actions after the goal was effectively achieved, resulting in unnecessarily low total reward.
task_instruction: Put the mug, squeezer, and toy food on the bench in the entryway.
